title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Food & Agriculture
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: French supermarket refrigeration attack: CERT-FR still says campaigns are probably ongoing, and Forescout counts nearly 13,000 exposed refrigeration services worldwide
items.content_text: Forescout reported on 22 October that it had found 12,976 internet-exposed refrigeration management services on 6,017 IP addresses in 99 countries, most of them from the Danfoss and Copeland/Dixell product families named in the French supermarket attack. Over the nights of 11–13 October, attackers remotely took over refrigeration controllers and forced continuous or extended defrost at about 700 French stores, according to Finance Minister Roland Lescure; Carrefour, Coopérative U, E.Leclerc, Intermarché/Netto and Monoprix confirmed impact, stock spoiled, and the Paris prosecutor reports fires. CERT-FR’s alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 names Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and, since 13 October, Copeland and Dixell XWEB supervisors; its latest version, from 16 October, still says the campaigns are “probably still ongoing,” though no new attack nights have been reported since 13 October. About 80% of the Danfoss StoreView services Forescout observed run firmware older than 4.3.1. No group has claimed the attacks, no entry route has been confirmed, and the prosecutor’s cybercrime section is investigating with OFAC and ANSSI.

_otthreatfeed.category: Top Story
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 (primary; v1 12 Oct, v2 13 Oct, v3 16 Oct, no later version as of 23 Oct); Forescout Vedere Labs (22 Oct); Waterfall Security (20 Oct); Finance Minister Lescure via AP (13 Oct); Danfoss and Copeland statements; SecurityWeek (15 Oct), The Hacker News, Reuters via Business Insurance, Le Monde Informatique (13 Oct)
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Attacks on the nights of 11–13 Oct 2026; CERT-FR alert last updated 16 Oct; Forescout exposure data 22 Oct 2026 — investigation ongoing

items.title: Ahold Delhaize confirms a malicious attack and restores online services; Albert Heijn home deliveries restart on 23 October
items.content_text: Ahold Delhaize said on 19 October that outside experts had confirmed the suspicious activity in its IT systems resulted from “malicious actions of others.” It notified the Dutch NCSC within 24 hours, has filed a police report and has no evidence so far that sensitive customer, associate or partner data was taken; all stores stayed open throughout. The company had taken systems offline as a precaution from 12 October, taking down websites and apps across most of its European and US brands, and an Albert Heijn statement reported by NL Times said its distribution centres had to be restarted on 13–14 October, leaving fresh-food shelves empty until deliveries resumed on 15 October. Albert Heijn’s website and app were back by 19 October and home deliveries restarted on 23 October (NL Times), with store replenishment still being scaled up; Stop & Shop and Hannaford were back online on 20 October, according to the company via the Boston Globe. No restoration status has been published for Food Lion or Giant. The company has not described the attack or said whether a ransom was involved, and no group has claimed it. Editorial assessment: this was an IT-side attack whose precautionary shutdown reached logistics; NL Times reports that electronic shelf labels showed wrong prices during the outage, but nothing shows refrigeration or other store OT was touched, and the Dutch NCSC said it did not believe the incident was linked to the French refrigeration attack.
tags: Incident — Grocery retail and distribution (Netherlands, Belgium, US); company-confirmed malicious attack on IT systems; not a confirmed OT compromise

items.title: FBI and Secret Service: the FortiBleed credential-theft campaign against Fortinet firewalls is still active, and food and agriculture is among its targets
items.content_text: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on Tuesday 6 October that the FortiBleed campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPNs remains active. There is no CVE: the attackers reuse leaked or stolen credentials, crack passwords kept in legacy SHA-256 storage and intercept authentication traffic, then add admin accounts and sometimes delete or reset the owners’ accounts, locking them out. The agencies say the targets span all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors, including energy and food and agriculture, and the FBI links the access to Payload ransomware; SOCRadar says it has confirmed at least 12 ransomware deployments from it. SOCRadar’s figure of 86,644 working device credentials across 194 countries dates from 19 June and is not a new count. No compromise of an OT system has been described. Editorial assessment: FortiGate firewalls often sit at the IT/OT boundary of processing plants and cold stores, so a hijacked admin account there can rewrite the segmentation that protects production.
tags: Active campaign — FortiGate firewall and SSL VPN credential theft (FBI/USSS); food and agriculture among targeted sectors; no CVE

items.title: Ukraine’s largest grocery chain, ATB, confirms a cyberattack; a data-theft claim by DataSuckers is disputed
items.content_text: ATB, which runs more than 1,300 stores, confirmed on 5 October that it had been hit by a cyberattack and took some online services offline, describing the website disruption as technical maintenance. It said a temporary message shown on its website did not affect the security of customer data and that the site remains fully under its control. A group calling itself DataSuckers claims to hold 7.9 million customer records, employee passport data and more than 11 million order records, has demanded $400,000, and says it will sell the data rather than leak it; ATB denies that customer data was compromised, and the claim has not been independently verified. The reporting describes no disruption to stores, logistics or payments, and no operational-technology impact has been reported. It remains IT-side and retail, and no later development was found by 23 October.
tags: Incident — Grocery retail, IT-side (website and online services); no OT impact reported

_otthreatfeed.category: Incident — Grocery retail, IT-side (website and online services); no OT impact reported
_otthreatfeed.source_name: ATB statements, as reported by The Record; DataSuckers’ claim (unverified)

items.title: Claroty: an AI coding agent rebuilt a root exploit for Danfoss refrigeration controllers in about 28 minutes
items.content_text: Prompted by the French attacks, Claroty’s Team82 reported on 13 October how quickly an AI coding agent could rebuild an exploit for Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws it had disclosed in August (CVE-2025-41450, -41451 and -41452). With a researcher steering it and a Ghidra integration, the agent reproduced the authentication bypass and chained it with command injection to gain root on a lab unit in about 28 minutes, for roughly US$6 of AI usage, using firmware anyone can download. Team82 stresses that the agent did not find the flaws on its own and does not say these flaws were used in France; ANSSI and Danfoss have not linked them to the attack either. Its point is that the time between disclosure and a working exploit may be shrinking. Editorial assessment: refrigeration and building controllers often run firmware years out of date, so faster exploit reproduction raises the cost of slow patching.
tags: Research — AI-assisted exploit reproduction against Danfoss refrigeration controllers (Claroty Team82); lab test only

_otthreatfeed.category: Research — AI-assisted exploit reproduction against Danfoss refrigeration controllers (Claroty Team82); lab test only

items.title: Nozomi: the French fridge attacks show why internet-reachable control interfaces are a standing risk
items.content_text: Nozomi Networks published an analysis on 13 October arguing that the French refrigeration attacks show what happens when control interfaces can be reached from the internet: anyone who gets to one can issue commands with physical effect. The exposure figures it uses are third-party counts: researcher Baptiste Robert found 2,752 internet-exposed Danfoss systems on 12 October, 1,590 of them in France, and Reuters saw at least 4,500 Danfoss interfaces on Shodan the next day. Separately, Censys saw French-exposed Danfoss StoreView panels fall from more than 1,800 on 11 October to 537 by 14 October while counts elsewhere barely moved (SecurityWeek). Nozomi recommends removing remote access that is not needed, putting the rest behind gateways with strong authentication, keeping a device and firmware inventory, watching for abnormal commands and spelling out contractor responsibilities. It names no attacker or entry route, and the post ends with a product pitch.
tags: Research — Vendor analysis of the French refrigeration attacks and internet-exposed OT (Nozomi Networks); no CVE

_otthreatfeed.category: Research — Vendor analysis of the French refrigeration attacks and internet-exposed OT (Nozomi Networks); no CVE
_otthreatfeed.source_name: Nozomi Networks blog (vendor analysis), citing Baptiste Robert and Reuters; Censys figures via SecurityWeek (15 Oct)

items.title: ESET: a Russian espionage group handed its access at a Ukrainian grain-logistics firm to Sandworm, which wiped data there in September 2025
items.content_text: ESET published research on 22 October about a 2025 attack, not a new one. UAC-0099, a Russia-aligned espionage group, phished its way into an unnamed Ukrainian grain-logistics company on 16 July 2025 and installed its MATCHBOIL downloader and MATCHWOK backdoor; a day later came MythicRatatoskr, a previously undocumented Go backdoor that reaches its command server over the Yggdrasil mesh network, which ESET calls the first documented abuse of Yggdrasil by a state-aligned actor. On 17 September 2025 the GRU-linked Sandworm group wiped data by pushing the legitimate SDelete utility through Active Directory Group Policy; ESET has high confidence in the handoff between the two groups. No operational-technology impact is described. According to The Record, ESET had already reported Sandworm wipers against Ukrainian grain organisations last year, so what is new is the handoff and the backdoor. Editorial assessment: no grain business outside Ukraine is named as a target, but the wipe needed no custom malware, only control of Group Policy, which makes Group Policy the asset to protect.
tags: Research — Destructive attack on a Ukrainian grain-logistics firm in September 2025 (ESET); IT-side data wipe; no OT impact reported

items.title: CISA, FBI and partners: SafePay ransomware has hit at least 600 organizations since August 2024, getting in through stolen VPN logins and edge-device flaws
items.content_text: Advisory AA26-293A, dated 20 October and co-sealed by CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service, Germany’s LKA Rheinland-Pfalz, the UK National Crime Agency and the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit, says SafePay has hit at least 600 organizations in multiple critical-infrastructure sectors since August 2024, in the Americas, Europe and Australia. SafePay, reported to operate as a closed group without affiliates, steals data and threatens to leak it as well as encrypting. It gets in with exposed or brute-forced credentials, VPN logins (notably from Mullvad addresses), phished accounts and automated exploitation of older edge-device flaws, including CVE-2020-3259 and CVE-2023-20269; once inside it uses WinRM, PsExec and RDP, moves data out with tools such as RClone, WinSCP and FileZilla, deletes shadow copies and resets NAS backup devices. The published coverage names no food or agriculture victims and describes no OT impact. Editorial assessment: food and agriculture is one of the critical-infrastructure sectors, and the NAS-reset step matters to plants that keep line, recipe or HMI backups on network storage.
tags: Joint advisory — SafePay ransomware (#StopRansomware AA26-293A); cross-sector; no food-sector victim named

items.title: CISA adds the BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day to KEV; Google says a suspected China-nexus espionage group exploited it from late August
items.content_text: Google Threat Intelligence Group said on 15 October that a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor it calls ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221) exploited a zero-day in BeyondTrust Remote Support from late August. The attackers gained root, harvested credentials, deleted logs and used the tool’s file transfer to pull documents from users’ desktops; SecurityWeek reports two appliances were compromised. BeyondTrust identified the flaw, CVE-2026-102764, on 28 September, shipped a fix on 8 October and patched its SaaS customers by 9 October; self-hosted customers without automatic updates must patch themselves. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 16 October with a 19 October deadline for federal agencies. GTIG names no victims or sectors and says any internet-reachable appliance that ran a vulnerable version during the window should be treated as possibly compromised and rebuilt. Editorial assessment: equipment makers and integrators often use remote-support tools like this to reach HMIs and engineering PCs in food plants.
tags: Active exploitation — Remote-support appliance zero-day (Google Threat Intelligence Group); in CISA KEV since 16 Oct; no OT or food victim named

items.title: Microsoft: one ransomware affiliate rotates Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT, and lists food and agriculture among victim sectors
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published a Storm-2570 profile on 24 September describing one affiliate that deployed four ransomware families — Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT — with largely the same toolkit: remote-management tools (MeshAgent, Atera, ScreenConnect, Splashtop, NinjaRMM), PsExec, Impacket and NetExec for lateral movement, Mimikatz-style credential theft, and s5cmd and Rclone for exfiltration. Microsoft lists food and agriculture among the affected sectors. Its recommended controls include tamper protection, attack surface reduction rules blocking PsExec and WMI lateral movement, MFA on approved remote-management tools, and credential resets if unauthorized installs appear.
tags: Threat actor profile — Cross-sector ransomware affiliate (IT-side)

_otthreatfeed.category: Threat actor profile — Cross-sector ransomware affiliate (IT-side)

items.title: Nozomi: the Cling botnet hides its command traffic in STUN requests and spreads through old router, camera and DVR flaws
items.content_text: Nozomi Networks Labs reported on 1 October that a botnet it calls Cling infects routers, access points, repeaters, DVRs and cameras, mainly through CVE-2021-35394 in the Realtek Jungle SDK, and carries exploits for seven other flaws, including CVE-2014-8361, CVE-2023-26801 and CVE-2024-3721. Infected devices contact public STUN servers, and the operators send commands encoded in STUN transaction IDs while spoofing source addresses so the traffic appears to come from Google’s STUN service. Nozomi saw the bots used for denial-of-service attacks on an internet provider, a university computing cluster and game servers; it gives no victim count and reports no OT or ICS compromise. Its advice is to patch the listed flaws, restrict inbound access and watch for unusual STUN patterns. Editorial assessment: low-cost routers, DVRs and cameras are common at farms, packhouses, grain sites and cold-storage warehouses, often on the same flat network as refrigeration or irrigation controllers.
tags: Research — IoT and edge-device botnet (Nozomi Networks Labs); no OT impact reported

items.title: Siemens Software Center flaw is exploited in a ClickFix malware campaign; CISA adds it to KEV with a 3 November deadline
items.content_text: Siemens confirmed on 19 October that attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS v3.1 6.7; v4.0 8.4) in Siemens Software Center, its tool for installing and updating Siemens software. The program did not restrict where it looks for helper DLLs, so attackers bundle a genuine, validly signed copy with their own DLLs and get victims to run the bundle through a ClickFix lure; Siemens ties the activity to what it calls the Romulus multi-platform ClickFix campaign and names no final malware family. Siemens says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached. Every version before V4.0.9.8 is affected; that version fixes the flaw, and existing installations update automatically on their next start. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 20 October with a 3 November federal deadline and republished Siemens’ advisory as ICSA-26-295-03 on 22 October. Editorial assessment: Siemens software is common on engineering workstations in food and beverage plants, where a signed Siemens program may not draw attention; the attack still needs a user to run the lure, so ClickFix awareness matters as much as the update.
tags: Active exploitation — Siemens Software Center DLL side-loading flaw (CVE-2026-110936) used in a ClickFix campaign; in CISA KEV; Windows PCs

items.title: PHP2Shell reaches OT products: Schneider, ABB and Moxa publish notices, and one Schneider engineering tool has no fix yet
items.content_text: Two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (“PHP2Shell”, CVSS v4.0 9.2 as rated by the PHP team), were fixed on 21 October in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 after details leaked early. Amazon says exploitation attempts began on 17 October, four days before the patches, and attempts now run into the millions, but no confirmed successful compromise has been reported and the flaws are not in CISA’s KEV catalog. Schneider Electric’s bulletin SESB-2026-295-01 (22 October) lists EcoStruxure Security Expert (fixed in 1.48.4.0), ProLeiT LINEoptimize, formerly Plant iT LMS (remediation through ProLeiT support), and every version of EcoStruxure Control Engineering, for which Schneider is still preparing a remediation plan. ABB has listed a notice on PHP2Shell’s impact on APROL (SA26P015), and Moxa has published a response (MPSA-260001). On 23 October PHP disclosed a further flaw, CVE-2026-115560, that applies only in an unusual configuration and is not fixed yet. Editorial assessment: any plant or production tool with a PHP web front end is a candidate, so the useful question for food processors is which of their suppliers’ products bundle PHP.

items.title: Ivanti Connect Secure: a three-flaw chain gave attackers root on fully patched VPNs, and one link has no patch yet
items.content_text: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that attackers chained three flaws in Connect Secure to get root on fully patched appliances. Two are fixed under a single CVE, CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS v3.1 8.6), an authentication bypass that leads to unauthenticated command execution; the third, a privilege escalation, has no CVE and no patch yet, with a fix promised in the coming weeks. Volexity found the chain during an incident response, tracks the actor as a new group, UTA0576, and with Defused dates exploitation to at least early October (1–3 October). The intruders stole domain credentials, pulled LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys from Active Directory, sprayed passwords and wiped logs, without leaving a web shell. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 13 October with a 16 October deadline and warns that Ivanti’s Integrity Checker may not detect the compromise. Editorial assessment: Connect Secure is a common remote-access path for plant engineers and equipment vendors, and stolen domain credentials can carry an intruder from the VPN toward plant systems.
tags: Active exploitation — Remote-access VPN; CVE-2026-104935 in CISA KEV; one chained flaw still unpatched

items.title: Citrix NetScaler: a fourth critical flaw follows three exploited zero-days, and some appliances patched last month need upgrading again
items.content_text: Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-107406 on 8 October (bulletin CTX697191), a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider that Citrix says may lead to code execution or denial of service. It is rated CVSS v4.0 9.5; no exploitation has been reported and it is not in CISA’s KEV catalog as of the 21 October release. Builds that fixed the late-September zero-days stay vulnerable when used as a SAML identity provider, so those appliances must be upgraded again. The three earlier flaws are exploited and in KEV: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (both CVSS v4 9.5, added 27 September) and CVE-2026-88779, which Citrix and watchTowr describe as a denial-of-service bug (added 4 October). Mandiant describes the attackers as suspected state-nexus, names no group and counts dozens of victim organizations in North America and Europe; Arctic Wolf counts at least 78 targeted organizations. Responders found custom web shells, and Mandiant warns that upgrading alone will not remove access already gained. Shadowserver counts more than 20,000 exposed or potentially vulnerable appliances. Editorial assessment: food and beverage plants commonly let integrators, co-packers and equipment vendors reach line controllers, refrigeration monitoring and batch systems through gateways like these.
tags: Active exploitation — Remote-access gateway; three flaws in CISA KEV, a fourth critical flaw patched 8 Oct

items.title: Fortinet FortiMail and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager zero-days are exploited in the wild; CISA lists both in KEV
items.content_text: Fortinet disclosed on 1 October that FortiMail CVE-2026-104286 (CVSS 9.8), a path-traversal flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files through crafted web requests, has been reported exploited in the wild; CISA added it to KEV the same day. Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2 and tells 7.2 users to move to 7.4 or later; disabling the IBE feature and limiting webmail access to trusted networks are interim workarounds. Cisco disclosed on 30 September that Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-76504 (CVSS 9.8) lets an unauthenticated attacker bypass API authentication and act as an administrator. Cisco says its PSIRT learned of active exploitation in September and that there are no workarounds; CISA added it to KEV on 30 September. Neither vendor has named an attacker or victims. Editorial assessment: processors and distributors with many plants and warehouses often link them over SD-WAN, and the mail gateway is a common starting point for phishing that ends in ransomware.

items.title: October OT patch day: Siemens S7-1500 web-server flaws with no fix yet, a Rockwell ArmorBlock takeover bug and an Ignition privilege escalation
items.content_text: Siemens’s 13 October release includes SSA-591731, eight web-server flaws in S7-1500, ET 200SP, ET 200pro and drive-controller CPUs (CVSS v3.1 9.6; all versions, no fix yet, mitigations only) that let an attacker run code in an authorized user’s browser and carry out PLC operations with that user’s rights. Siemens also lists 377 CVEs in the optional Linux subsystem of the S7-1500 TM MFP module (no fix yet) and an authenticated path-traversal flaw in Industrial Edge devices (CVE-2026-44415, CVSS v3.1 9.1). Rockwell’s SD1801 covers 1732E ArmorBlock I/O modules on firmware 3.012 and earlier: CVE-2026-12655 (CVSS v3.1 9.1) lets an unauthenticated attacker change the web-server password and take over the module, and CVE-2026-12656 is a network-storm denial of service that needs a power cycle; the fix is 3.013. CISA’s 13 October advisory for Inductive Automation Ignition (CVE-2026-92817, 8.8) covers a privilege escalation fixed in 8.1.55 and 8.3.9, and Schneider flagged Pro-face STW6000/Harmony STW6 HMIs (CVE-2026-96434, 8.8). None is reported exploited or listed in KEV. CISA republished Siemens’ advisories on 22 October (ICSA-26-295-02 to -18); the S7 web-server and TM MFP issues still have no fix. Editorial assessment: S7-1500 CPUs, ArmorBlock I/O and Ignition are widely used on food and beverage processing and packaging lines.
tags: Advisory — Siemens, Rockwell, Inductive Automation and Schneider October releases; no known exploitation

items.title: IO-Link masters from three vendors share about 20 flaws, two rated CVSS 9.8; Nozomi details the attack chain
items.content_text: CERT@VDE published three advisories on 16 September — VDE-2026-014 (Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3), VDE-2026-027 (Phoenix Contact IOL MA8) and VDE-2026-028 (Carlo Gavazzi YL212/YN115) — covering the same firmware family (versions below 1.7.4) and roughly 20 CVEs each, including two rated CVSS 9.8: an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-27546) and a malicious file upload leading to root code execution (CVE-2026-27565); ten more score 8.8. On 24 September Nozomi Networks Labs published a write-up of the Pepperl+Fuchs master, showing that chained together the flaws give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device. All three vendors point to firmware 1.7.8. No exploitation has been reported. Editorial assessment: IO-Link masters sit at the sensor and actuator layer of packaging, filling and dosing lines.
tags: Advisory — Field-I/O firmware, about 20 CVEs, no known exploitation

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Field-I/O firmware, about 20 CVEs, no known exploitation
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CERT@VDE advisories VDE-2026-014, -027 and -028 (primary); Nozomi Networks Labs

items.title: CISA: a command-injection flaw lets low-privileged users get root on WAGO PFC and CC100 controllers; Moxa’s AIG-302 gateway has a hard-coded key
items.content_text: CISA’s 20 October batch republished WAGO advisory VDE-2026-096 as ICSA-26-293-02, covering CC100, PFC100 G2, PFC200 G2, TP600, Edge Controller and WP400 devices on firmware older than 4.10.0 (FW32). CVE-2026-80466 (CVSS v3.1 8.8) lets a low-privileged remote user inject operating-system commands through routing parameters in the web-based management, which a helper then runs as root; CVE-2026-88850 (v3.1 8.1) lets low-privileged users change root-owned PROFIBUS settings. Firmware 4.10.0 (FW32) fixes both. The same batch covers Moxa’s AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge gateway (ICSA-26-293-03): a hard-coded cryptographic key, CVE-2026-109813 (v3.1 8.1; v4.0 8.6), and a missing-authorization flaw, both fixed in firmware 1.4.1. Neither is reported exploited, and both are separate from the WAGO BACnet flaw disclosed on 1 October (below). Editorial assessment: WAGO PFC controllers are common in food-plant utilities, refrigeration plant and building control, so until the update is in, any valid web-management login on them should be treated as a root login.
tags: Advisory — WAGO controllers and a Moxa edge gateway (CISA, 20 Oct); no known exploitation

items.title: CERT@VDE: a CVSS 9.8 flaw in the BACnet stack of WAGO controllers, plus CODESYS runtime fixes for WAGO and other PLCs
items.content_text: CERT@VDE published WAGO advisory VDE-2025-102 on 1 October for CVE-2025-41753 (CVSS 9.8), a path-traversal flaw in the BACnet/IP stack: by giving BACnet File Objects names that act as file paths, an unauthenticated attacker can read or overwrite arbitrary files, which can lead to full compromise of the device. It affects 750-811x, 750-821x, 751-9x01 and 752-8303 controllers and 762-series panels on firmware below 4.8.9 (FW30). A second WAGO advisory the same day (VDE-2025-081) covers CODESYS runtime flaws in the same families that let an unauthenticated attacker crash the device (the highest, CVE-2025-41738, is CVSS 8.3), plus a manipulated project file that can run code if a user opens it; the fix is firmware 4.10.0 (FW32). On 30 September CODESYS fixed a runtime race condition, CVE-2026-79625 (CVSS 8.1, needs authenticated monitoring access), in 3.5.22.40, with Linux-based variants due in 4.23.0.0 in the fourth quarter. No exploitation is reported for any of them. Editorial assessment: WAGO controllers and CODESYS-based PLCs are common in food-processing automation, refrigeration plant control and building management, where BACnet is the usual building-systems protocol.

items.title: OT Cybersecurity Coalition: the French attack came from missed basics, and US refrigeration controllers could be next
items.content_text: The Operational Technology Cybersecurity Coalition said in a 14 October statement that failures in basic cybersecurity practice led to a significant incident in France, repeated ANSSI’s advice on VPN-only access, default passwords and firmware updates, and warned that attackers could treat refrigeration controllers in the US as a way in, while noting that no US incidents have been reported. It renewed its 6 October call for CISA to issue a binding operational directive on OT security at federal civilian agencies, with an accountable OT security officer and minimum practices drawn from existing federal guidance, citing a GAO finding that only 7 of 22 large civilian agencies fully met OMB’s networked-device requirements. CISA has announced no directive. A directive would bind federal agencies, not private food companies.

items.title: CIRCIA final rule reaches White House review; 72-hour incident and 24-hour ransom-payment reporting still awaits its start dates
items.content_text: CISA sent its final rule under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act to the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs, which logged it for review on 1 October. The law sets 72-hour reporting of covered cyber incidents and 24-hour reporting of ransom payments for covered entities in the 16 critical-infrastructure sectors, which include food and agriculture, but obligations begin only on dates the final rule sets, and who is covered depends on that rule, whose text is not yet public. The statutory deadline passed in October 2025 and later targets slipped; HIPAA Journal reports publication is expected before the end of the year. The text can still change during review, and no final rule had been published as of 23 October.

items.title: CISA and the FBI urge critical-infrastructure operators to put ICS integrators on least privilege and monitored remote access
items.content_text: CISA and the FBI released a fact sheet, dated 23 September and reported on 24 September, on the risks of working with third-party ICS integrators. It cites an FBI-analyzed intrusion at a US industrial automation firm in March–April 2025 in which foreign actors took roughly 800 files, including customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics. Recommendations: assess what data integrators hold, apply least privilege, secure and monitor remote connections, keep offline backups, write cybersecurity requirements into contracts, disconnect public-facing devices, and weigh geopolitical factors for foreign-owned providers. Coverage names power utilities and transportation as the firm’s customers; the fact sheet does not single out food and agriculture. Editorial assessment: food plants rely on integrators for line controls, batch systems and refrigeration, so the same exposure applies.
